parties.counterparty: Manufacturers' Services Western U.S. Operations, Inc. (MSL)

plans.note: Primary text is Base Agreement 15.3 (Limitations of Liability) within Section 15.0; check mutuality, the cap amount/formula, and carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, bodily injury/property damage, gross negligence). Also review Section 15 (Limitation of Remedies) and Section 13 (Disclaimer of Warranty) of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement, which run in IBM's favour as lender and should not be flagged.

MSL's indemnity is at 15.1 (Scope of MSL's Indemnity) with procedure at 15.2 (Payment and Cooperation). Confirm coverage of third-party IP claims, personal injury/property damage and MSL misconduct, and that any reciprocal IBM indemnity (including IP arising from IBM-supplied designs) stays narrow; cross-check IP provisions in 13.0 and Section 14 of the loan agreement.

Scan Scope of Work (3.0), Prohibited Suppliers (16.15) and Integration Restrictions and Limitations (14.18) for any covenant limiting IBM's ability to manufacture or source competing products; outsourcing agreements of this type usually restrict the supplier, not the customer, so likely absent.

Look for any sole-source or requirements language in Scope of Work (3.0), Purchase of Products (6.0 of the Product Attachment), Product Forecast (11.0) and Parts purchasing (8.1); confirm IBM retains the right to source elsewhere and that forecasts are non-binding.

Pricing sits in Section 7.0 (Price), 8.2 (Parts Cost Reductions), 14.14 (Integration Price) and Appendix 1 (Mark Up); check for any best-price/most-favoured-customer obligation running against IBM. Any MFN favouring IBM is beneficial and should not be flagged.

Personnel (Section 9.0) governs transferred employees and is the likely home of any hiring/solicitation restriction on IBM; verify scope, duration and a general-advertising carve-out, and note that restrictions running only against MSL are not flagged.

Termination architecture is Section 5.0 (Breach, Rights Upon Termination, Prices Upon Termination) read with Term (4.0 Base / 2.0 Product Attachment) and Purchase Order cancellation (6.1). Check whether IBM has a convenience right, the notice period, any wind-down/inventory or price-uplift charges on exit, and whether MSL holds a symmetrical walk-away.

Term clauses at Base 4.0 and Product Attachment 2.0 should show whether renewal is automatic or by agreement, the non-renewal notice window, and any pricing on extension (5.3 addresses prices upon termination/extension).

Section 16.9 (Governing Law) is the operative clause; confirm the chosen state (New York/Delaware/California acceptable) and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration. Check the general sections of the EOCI (Section 8) and loan agreement (Section 16) for conflicting law/venue terms.

Assignment (16.2) plus Sale or Merger (16.5) control transfer and change of control; verify IBM may assign to affiliates/successors without consent and that MSL cannot terminate or reprice on an IBM change of control. Assignees and Visits (16.7) may bear on subcontracting.

Section 13.0 (Intellectual and Industrial Property) with 13.3 (Licenses) is the core; confirm IBM retains ownership of its IP, tooling (20.0/21.1) and confidential data, and that nothing assigns IBM IP or IBM-funded developments to MSL. Ownership and License (Section 5) and Licensed Internal Code (Section 6) of the loan agreement are supporting.

Licences granted to IBM (if any) would sit in 13.3; check scope, revocability, and extension to IBM Related Companies and contractors. Most licence flow here runs from IBM to MSL (Attachment 6 software terms, loan agreement Sections 5–6, I/T system access 24.1) — restrictions on MSL are favourable to us.

Section 7.0 (Audit), 16.14 (Records), Attachment 6 Section 4.0 (Additional Audit Rights) and Appendix A Section 4 run in IBM's favour as auditor and should not be redlined; flag only any reciprocal right for MSL to audit IBM's premises, records or usage, checking notice, frequency and cost allocation.

Look for charges payable by IBM: Premium Cost (9.0), cancellation/rescheduling charges (6.1), EOL and excess inventory liability (13.3/13.4), supply flexibility (13.2) and requirements-accuracy penalties (Appendix 2). Delivery-performance mechanics at 10.2/10.4 and shipment profit-rate deductions operate against MSL and are welcome.

MSL's warranties are at Base 14.2 and Product Attachment Section 19 (scope, exclusions, turnaround, epidemic failure), with Attachment 6 Section 3.0 additional software warranties. Check warranty duration, the repair/replace remedy and turnaround commitment, the implied-warranty disclaimer at 19.6, and the survival limit at 16.19.

No insurance heading appears in the General section (16.1–16.21) or elsewhere; check Risk of Loss or Damage (loan agreement Section 8), Lease of Premises (10.0) and Care of tooling (21.2) for any embedded coverage obligation before treating the rule as missing.

Check Purchase of Products (6.0), Product Forecast (11.0/11.3), Supply Flexibility (13.2) and Requirements Accuracy (Appendix 2) for volume commitments or forecast-liability that operates as take-or-pay on IBM, and whether an exit or cancellation right exists.

Transition Services (Section 12.0) plus Rights Upon Termination (5.2) and Prices Upon Termination (5.3) should carry exit assistance; also check inventory/tooling repurchase (13.4, 21.0), return of loaned items (Section 12 of the loan agreement) and obligations upon termination in Attachment 6 Section 3 for return of IBM materials and data.
